sources.reading_verification: Downloaded the complete 166-page v3.08 PDF and extracted its full text with mutool. Inspected the complete Ch. 5 unit-theorem chapter on printed pp.85-94 (Lemmas 5.1-5.2, Examples 5.3-5.4, Prop. 5.5, Cor. 5.6, Prop. 5.8, Thm. 5.9, Lemma 5.10, the S-unit section with Thm. 5.11, the CM-field and continuous-fraction examples, Lemma 5.13, and the Regulators section), Ch. 4 pp.73-75 (Lemma 4.14, Prop. 4.15), Ch. 7 pp.112-113 (Thm. 7.15, Lemma 7.16, Remark 7.17) and Ch. 8 pp.137-139 (Prop. 8.7, Thm. 8.8, Aside 8.9). Milne writes the log map with doubled complex coordinates in Thm. 5.9's proof and in the Regulators normalization, which is the convention this batch adopts.

contents.name: Lemma 5.1 (a number field contains only finitely many roots of unity)
contents.support: The degree divisibility phi(m) | [K:Q] bounds the possible orders; the scaffold's proof reaches the same finiteness through the bounded-conjugate polynomial box supplied in-run by batch 2.

contents.name: Lemma 5.2 (a in O_K is a unit if and only if Nm(a) = +-1)
Example 5.3 (d < 0: the norm equations have finitely many solutions and mu(K) is listed for Q(i), Q(sqrt(-3)))
contents.support: The d < 0 paragraph and the mu(K) list are exactly the zero-rank B-page cases.

contents.name: Example 5.3 (d > 0: U_K = +-u^Z for a fundamental unit u)
contents.support: The d > 0 paragraph identifies the unit group as generated by one fundamental unit; the B page relates the norm-one part to the Pell generator of the order.

contents.name: Example 5.4 (cubic K = Q(alpha), alpha^3+10alpha+1 = 0, discriminant -4027, rank one)
contents.reason: A rank-one cubic with one real and one complex place used to illustrate a root of the minimum polynomial as a unit; the B page's cubic example is totally real of rank two, so this illustration is not built.

contents.name: Proposition 5.5 (finitely many algebraic integers of degree at most m with all conjugates bounded by M)
contents.support: This bounded-coefficients finiteness is the batch-2 supplier lem-bounded-conjugates-give-finitely-many-integral-polynomials, which both finiteness proofs of this batch consume as an examined prerequisite.

contents.name: Corollary 5.6 (an algebraic integer each of whose conjugates has absolute value 1 is a root of unity)
Remark 5.7 ((3+4i)/5 shows the algebraic-integrality hypothesis cannot be dropped)
contents.reason: A sharpness remark about the integrality hypothesis; the page states the criterion for algebraic integers and does not build a separate non-integral counterexample.

contents.name: The log map L and the hyperplane H (coordinate sum with doubled complex weights)
contents.support: The doubled complex coordinate displayed for L is exactly the convention fixed by the logarithmic embedding definition.

contents.name: Proposition 5.8(a) (the image of L restricted to units is a lattice in H)
Proposition 5.8(b) (the kernel of L is finite, hence equals mu(K))
Theorem 5.9 (the image of L is a full lattice; U_K has rank r+s-1)
Lemma 5.10 (a real matrix with negative off-diagonal entries and positive row sums is invertible)
contents.reason: Milne's final invertibility step for the independence matrix of the units epsilon_i; the scaffold instead follows Stein's equivalent fixed-product adjustment for the same covering argument, so this lemma is neither needed nor restated.

contents.name: The S-units section: the ring O_K(S) of S-integers and the group U(S) of S-units
Theorem 5.11 (the S-unit group has rank r+s+#S-1; p_i^h = (pi_i) supplies rank #S)
The worked instance K = Q with S = {(2),(3),(5)}: U(S) = {+-2^k 3^m 5^n}
CM fields: Proposition 5.12 (the index of mu(K)U_{K+} in U_K is 1 or 2)
contents.reason: CM-field unit theory is a separate arithmetic topic that the unit theorem's rank and regulator do not require; the page records the rank formula only and does not build the CM index statement.

contents.name: Example: real quadratic fields via continued fractions (sqrt(94), sqrt(9199))
contents.reason: Continued fractions are an algorithm for finding the fundamental unit; the page identifies the fundamental unit through the published Pell classification and does not develop the continued-fraction method.

contents.name: Example: cubic fields with negative discriminant; Lemma 5.13 (|d_K| < 4 eps^3 + 24)
contents.reason: A lower bound relating the fundamental unit to the discriminant in the rank-one cubic case; the design deliberately omits regulator lower bounds and no consumer in the pair uses this inequality.

contents.name: Regulators: the vectors l(u_i) and the regulator determinant of a fundamental system
The regulator of an arbitrary independent system and the index ratio |Reg(eps_i)| / |Reg(U)|
contents.support: The index-ratio discussion is the conceptual form of the GL_r(Z) change-of-system invariance that the well-definedness theorem proves.

contents.name: Lemma 4.14 (a subgroup meets every bounded set finitely if and only if it is discrete)
Proposition 4.15 (a subgroup of V is a lattice if and only if it is discrete)
Theorem 7.15 (product formula) with Lemma 7.16(b) (the local norm identity over the primes above v)
Remark 7.17 (product formula for function fields and other completions)
contents.reason: Function-field and non-number-field completions lie outside this pair's scope; the page normalizes only the number-field places its arguments use.

contents.name: Proposition 8.7 (the product of the local normalized absolute values computes |Nm_{L/K}|)
contents.support: The extension/normalization identity is used for the archimedean norm comparison and is absorbed into the product-formula item.

contents.name: Theorem 8.8 (product formula for an algebraic number field)
Aside 8.9 (Artin-Whaples axiomatic characterization of global fields)
contents.reason: An axiomatic characterization of global fields by a product-formula condition; the pair uses the product formula itself and no clause of the characterization.

contents.name: Definition 8.1.1 (the unit group U_K of a number field)

contents.name: Theorem 8.1.2 (Dirichlet: U_K is finite cyclic times free abelian of rank r+s-1, via a covering of H)

contents.name: Lemma 8.1.9 (the image phi(U_K) is discrete)

canonical.name: Deleted-row minors: for a rank-m (m+1)x m real matrix with zero column sums, Delta_k = (-1)^(k-1) Delta_1 and every Delta_k is nonzero
canonical.support: Local technical lemma added in this dispatch; it is not a source heading. The underlying statement is quoted by Milne, Algebraic Number Theory v3.08, Ch. 5 p.94 (the regulator is computed from any one deleted coordinate, the choice immaterial) and by Sutherland's 18.785 Lecture 15, Definition 15.16 p.9 (every minor of the log matrix has the same absolute value); the repeated-column/rank-nullity proof recorded in the item is local. Consumed by def-number-field-regulator and thm-number-field-regulator-is-well-defined.
